sets.title: RC: E-commerce in India
sets.context:
Over the past decade, e-commerce has transformed the way Indians shop, turning what was once a niche convenience into a mainstream habit. The proliferation of affordable smartphones and cheap mobile data has brought millions of first-time buyers online, many of them from small towns that traditional retail chains had long **overlooked**. For these consumers, the digital marketplace offers not merely lower prices but access to a range of goods that local stores could never stock. Analysts estimate that the sector will continue to expand at a brisk pace, driven as much by rising aspirations as by improving logistics.

Yet the growth has not been without friction. Small brick-and-mortar retailers, who form the backbone of the country's vast unorganised retail economy, complain that deep-pocketed online platforms lure customers with steep discounts that no independent shopkeeper can match. Regulators, too, have grown **wary** of practices that may distort competition, and successive policy revisions have sought to curb predatory pricing while protecting the interests of small vendors. The platforms counter that they generate employment, widen markets for domestic manufacturers, and pass on genuine efficiencies to consumers.

The pandemic accelerated these trends dramatically. With physical stores shuttered during lockdowns, even reluctant shoppers were **compelled** to buy essentials online, and habits formed out of necessity have proved surprisingly durable. Grocery, once considered too perishable and low-margin for online sale, emerged as one of the fastest-growing categories. Still, profitability remains elusive for most players, who continue to burn cash in pursuit of market share. Whether the industry can convert its impressive scale into sustainable returns is, in the end, the question on which its future hinges.

sets.title: Cloze: Financial Literacy
sets.context: Financial literacy is increasingly regarded as an essential life skill. As economies grow more complex, individuals are expected to make decisions that were once ___(1)___ to a small group of specialists. A person who does not understand how interest ___(2)___ over time, or how inflation erodes the value of savings, is poorly ___(3)___ to plan for the future. Unfortunately, surveys reveal that a large ___(4)___ of the population lacks even a basic grasp of these concepts. Experts argue that schools should ___(5)___ financial education into their curricula, so that young people acquire these skills before they enter the workforce. Such an approach, they believe, would ___(6)___ households against the kind of costly mistakes that often lead to debt.

sets.title: Para Jumble: The Shift to Clean Energy
sets.context:
Six sentences are given below, labelled P, Q, R, S, T and U. When rearranged, they form a coherent paragraph.
P: For decades, fossil fuels powered the engines of industrial growth across the world.
Q: However, the environmental costs of burning coal and oil soon became impossible to ignore.
R: Scientists warned that rising carbon emissions were steadily warming the planet.
S: In response, governments began investing heavily in cleaner sources of energy.
T: Today, solar and wind power are among the fastest-growing industries on earth.
U: Their falling costs suggest that a cleaner future may be closer than many once believed.
